purpose: Add explicit routed and policy-enforced OT network fidelity without replacing the stable Docker Compose experiment baseline.

topology_orchestrator.name: Containerlab
topology_orchestrator.lifecycle_rule: Containerlab must not become the lifecycle owner of canonical Compose services
topology_orchestrator.reconciliation_rule: Any runtime implementation must prove interface restoration after Compose container restart before daemon acceptance

routing.dynamic_routing_admission_rule: Add FRR only if a documented experiment or learning objective requires a routing protocol

policy_enforcement.policy: default deny with explicit stateful permits derived from declared conduits
policy_enforcement.claim_boundary: This is a software policy-enforcement point, not a vendor industrial-firewall appliance and not an IEC/IACS compliance claim

passive_visibility.baseline: namespace/interface capture already present in the Compose lab
passive_visibility.admission_rule: Add OVS only when an experiment explicitly requires passive mirrored traffic rather than capture at a known endpoint/interface

not_selected_as_reference.reason: Useful network emulation platform, but its Docker mode treats containers as lightweight virtual machines and is not designed to manage the existing Compose container infrastructure.
Useful for vendor virtual appliances, but it adds QEMU/vendor-image lifecycle and licensed-image burden that is not required for the current open reproducible experiment baseline.
Does not solve the current single-host network-fidelity requirement and would add CNI/Service abstractions to packet ground truth.
Static inter-zone routing is sufficient unless dynamic-routing behavior becomes an explicit experiment.

design_invariants: The existing Compose baseline remains independently startable, testable, and publishable.
No second source of truth for current OT endpoint IP addresses is introduced; docker-compose.yml and security/conduits.json remain authoritative.
Every newly permitted routed flow must map to a documented conduit and have an explicit protocol/port purpose.
Default-deny behavior must be demonstrated by both a permitted-flow test and a denied-flow test.
Control traffic and supervisory traffic must remain distinguishable in packet evidence.
The extension must preserve deterministic source/destination identities needed by experiment evaluators.
A service or link being up is not acceptance; evidence must prove policy, path, capture, restart, and recovery behavior.
No vendor firewall behavior, class approval, IEC 62443 compliance, or IACS compliance is claimed from Linux/nftables/Containerlab emulation.

runtime_acceptance_gates.name: baseline isolation
runtime_acceptance_gates.pass_condition: Canonical Compose baseline passes its existing Gates A-G without the network-fidelity extension enabled.

runtime_acceptance_gates.name: deterministic attachment
runtime_acceptance_gates.pass_condition: Extension attaches only declared interfaces and preserves deterministic experiment identities.

runtime_acceptance_gates.name: default deny
runtime_acceptance_gates.pass_condition: An undeclared inter-zone flow is denied and logged while every declared required conduit remains functional.

runtime_acceptance_gates.name: path evidence
runtime_acceptance_gates.pass_condition: PCAP and policy logs prove the expected routed path for at least one Modbus and one OPC UA flow.

runtime_acceptance_gates.name: restart reconciliation
runtime_acceptance_gates.pass_condition: After a selected Compose service restarts, required extension interfaces/routes/policies are restored without changing the canonical IP/conduit ground truth.

runtime_acceptance_gates.name: failure and recovery
runtime_acceptance_gates.pass_condition: A gateway/policy-enforcement failure produces the documented operational evidence and recovery restores the expected path.

runtime_acceptance_gates.name: passive visibility
runtime_acceptance_gates.pass_condition: If SPAN/mirroring is enabled, the sensor receives a copy of the selected traffic without becoming an inline forwarding dependency.
